hero.title: Robotics on the biggest stage in the state.
hero.subtitle: This was our fifth year bringing live robotics and fabrication demos to the Milwaukee Maker Faire at Discovery World, one of the largest maker events in the country. Six thousand attendees, five hundred conversations, one stage we keep getting invited back to.

impact.label: Why it matters
impact.text: Maker Faire doesn't re-invite teams out of courtesy — it invites back the ones that pull crowds and leave people with something real. Getting asked back five years running tells us what we're doing works. In year four it even gave us a new team member: a visitor got hooked on our CNC demo and ended up joining.

approach.label: Our Approach
approach.heading: What We Bring to Maker Faire

inlinePhoto.caption: GEarheads booth setup at Discovery World, full floor view

approach.body:
Most teams at Maker Faire bring a poster and a robot on a table. We bring a working fabrication shop — a CNC machine cutting real parts, a full competition robot people can drive, and members who treat a twelve-year-old's 'how does it know where to go?' with the same seriousness as an engineer's question about feedrates.

We brief the team before each day: rotate stations, read the crowd, meet people where they are. Ten seconds for someone passing by, twenty minutes for someone who wants the whole G-code pipeline. The crowd is exactly who we want to reach — families whose kids haven't found FIRST yet, hobbyist machinists, teachers, engineers curious about the next generation. Everyone leaves with something: info on joining FIRST, our MPCNC build guide, or just a better sense of what student robotics looks like.

highlights.title: Discovery World — The Third Largest Maker Faire in the US
highlights.description:
Discovery World isn't a local craft show — it's one of the top three Maker Faires in the country by attendance, drawing makers and families from across the Midwest. Our booth sits on the lakefront alongside CNC shops, textile hackers, and giant 3D printers.

That mix keeps us honest — engineers, parents scouting STEM programs, and middle schoolers all end up at our table, sometimes in the same conversation. You can't fake your way through this crowd; you have to actually know your stuff.

highlights.title: CNC and MPCNC Live Machining on the Floor
highlights.description:
Our flagship demo is a live MPCNC (Mostly Printed CNC) cutting real toolpaths on the floor — the same machine we teach other FTC teams to build in our DIY-CNC program. Watching a router bit trace a path through wood or acrylic answers 'what does a robotics team actually build?' better than any slide.

We talk through the design, how the toolpaths come out of Fusion 360, and how the same logic builds parts on Gearboticus, our competition robot. Since it's mostly 3D-printed parts and hardware-store hardware, it's replicable — every team that sees it is a potential future DIY-CNC teammate.

highlights.title: Full FTC Robot Demo and Hands-On Driving
highlights.description:
We bring Gearboticus, our full competition robot, and let attendees drive it. Nothing beats holding a controller and moving a 30-pound robot yourself.

Members walk through each subsystem — the sweeping intake, the spindexer, the flywheel launcher, the mecanum drivetrain — and why we built them that way. Kids load a scoring element and watch it fire; parents ask about navigation or what a two-week sprint looks like. It's a real conversation, not a pitch — and it's not a kit, it's a machine we designed, built, and competed with at the FIRST World Championship.

highlights.title: 500+ Conversations Across Two Days
highlights.description:
Across both days we talk to more than five hundred people — not just passersby, but people who stopped, asked questions, or stuck around for a full demo. We rotate members all weekend so everyone gets a student who's excited to talk.

Families with middle schoolers get pointed toward FIRST team-finding resources. Curious adults get our MPCNC build docs. Kids who want to drive get a member at the controller. It's recruitment and community-building, and we treat it like one.

highlights.title: From Attendee to Team Member — The Recruiting Story
highlights.description:
In our fourth year, a visitor got stuck at the CNC table — he wanted to know the feedrate, the CAM software, how the same logic showed up in the robot next to it. He wasn't a kid looking for a club; he was someone curious about fabrication who found a student team doing it more seriously than he expected.

By the end he had our contact info. He came to a meeting, joined, and is now on both the mechanical and software subteams. It's one story out of five hundred conversations, but it's the one that shows what we're actually trying to do: build a front door worth walking through.

recruitingCallout.label: The moment it clicked
recruitingCallout.title: A visitor walked up to the CNC machine and never really left.
recruitingCallout.text: He stood at our table for forty minutes asking about feedrates, toolpaths, and how a machine built mostly from printed parts cuts metal. By the end he had our contact info. He came to a meeting the next week, joined, and is now active on both mechanical and software. One good conversation turned into a teammate.

partners.name: Milwaukee Maker Faire at Discovery World
partners.note: Third-largest Maker Faire in the US by attendance, held annually at the Discovery World science and technology museum on the Milwaukee lakefront. GEarheads has exhibited five years running.
